translations.text: saying thus: "I saw so great a multitude that no one can number it, from all nations and from every tribe, standing before God's throne,
all clothed in white garments, holding palm branches in their hands, and they sang with a loud voice: 'Salvation be to our God, who sits upon his throne.'
They were God's spokesmen, and to them he revealed his secrets. He enlightened them with the grace of the Holy Spirit, so that they knew the things to come and proclaimed them in prophetic song.
Truly, the chosen prophets shone in their lives through many signs and prefigurations. They healed people's sicknesses and raised the bodies of the dead to life.
Taught by the Holy Spirit, they prophesied Christ's incarnation, his passion, his resurrection, his ascension, and the great judgment.
In the New Testament came John the Baptist, who proclaimed Christ's coming by prophecy and also pointed him out with his finger.
"Among those born of women there has not risen anyone greater than John the Baptist."
With these champions of God agrees the twelvefold number of Christ's apostles, whom he himself chose as his disciples and trained in right faith and true teaching,
After the company of the apostles we honour the steadfast host of God's martyrs, who bravely imitated Christ's passion through various torments and went to the heavenly kingdom through martyrdom.
Some were killed with weapons, some burned up in flames, others beaten with whips, others pierced with stakes,
some tormented by winter cold, some killed by hunger, and some had their hands and feet cut off as a spectacle for the people, for the faith and for the holy name of Christ the Saviour.
They also offered themselves to God as a living sacrifice, without blemish or any mixture of perverse work.
After these follows the way of life of the anchorites, with their singular devotion. Living in deserts, they trampled down worldly pleasures and lusts with strong minds and strict lives.
They fled from the sight and praise of worldly people. Hiding in poor caves or huts, they lived alongside wild beasts and grew used to speaking with angels, and they shone with great miracles.
They gave sight to the blind, the power to walk to the lame, hearing to the deaf, and speech to the mute. They overcame devils and drove them out, and through God's power they raised the dead.
The book called Vitae Patrum (Lives of the Fathers) speaks at length about the way of life of these anchorites, and also of monks living in community, and says,

and holy conduct, and modest clothing, so much so that a great many of them suffered martyrdom for the sake of their virginity, and so, with a twofold victory, they came in glory to the heavenly dwellings.
When he had sat down, his disciples came to him, and he opened his mouth and taught them, saying: "Blessed are the poor in spirit," and so on.
Yet it was the one God who, through his holy prophets, set the lesser commandments for the Jewish people, who were still bound by fear;

and through his own Son he set the greater commandments for the Christian people, whom he came to redeem out of true love. He taught while sitting, which belongs to the dignity of the teacher's office.
In this way Abraham was poor, and Jacob, and David, who, though raised up on his royal throne, showed himself to be poor in spirit, saying thus: "Truly I am needy and poor."
The proud rich are not poor, neither through want nor in spirit, because they are enriched with possessions and puffed up in mind.
but those are blessed who bewail their sins, because the Holy Spirit, who grants forgiveness of all sins, comforts them,
he will then be filled with the food of which the Lord spoke: "My food is that I do my Father's will"; that is, righteousness.
Then he may say with the psalmist: "Lord, I shall appear with righteousness in your sight, and I shall be filled when your glory is revealed."
"Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God."
